_comment: Egress schedules for providers with no machine-readable pricing endpoint.
AWS and Azure are NOT here — they are collected live (see pipeline/collectors/egress.mjs).
Every entry needs a human pass against source_url before launch; until then
source_verified_at stays null and the UI badges the row as unverified.
'bundled_with_compute: true' means the real allowance is per-plan on the compute
record (included_egress_gb) and these tiers price the OVERAGE only.

notes: Premium network tier (the default). Standard tier is cheaper but routes over the public internet sooner.
Rates vary by destination continent; these are the North America / Europe figures.
10 TB/month free account-wide, then a flat rate — by far the most generous hyperscaler allowance.
This single line is why OCI wins most egress-heavy comparisons.
EU plans bundle ~20 TB/month; overage is billed at EUR 1.00/TB (~$0.00108/GB).
US locations (Ashburn, Hillsboro) bundle less traffic than EU locations — verify per location.
Roughly 80x cheaper per GB than AWS on-demand egress.
Each Droplet adds its allowance to a shared account-wide pool.
Allowances pool across all Linodes in the account.
R2 charges zero egress. Unlimited, not an allowance — the structural outlier.
Storage and Class A/B operations are still billed.
Object storage only; there is no Cloudflare VM to attach this to.
Free egress up to 3x the average monthly stored bytes, then $0.01/GB.
The 3x allowance is storage-dependent, so it cannot be modelled as a flat free tier — treated as $0.01/GB throughout, which OVERSTATES cost for most workloads.
Free entirely to Cloudflare and other Bandwidth Alliance partners.
